AMIGO Municipal Vice-Mayor Municipality of Molave Province of Zamboanga del Sur Dear VM Amigo: This has reference to your letter dated 29 January 2018 requesting for this Department's legal opinion relative to the Memorandum No. 0229, S. 2017 issued by Mayor Ireneo Glepa, informing you that all Job Order (JO) contracts in the Office of the Sangguniang Bayan will be signed by the Mayor as the approving authority, and with the Vice-Mayor (V M) as requestor. The said Memorandum is anchored on DILG Legal Opinion Number 17, S. 2010 dated 8 March 2010, wherein, the Department has previously opined that the Mayor has the authority to hire JOS regardless of the source of their salaries. Per your letter, you posed the following queries which we quoted hereunder: 1. Whether the Vice Mayor has the authority to hire Job Order Workers/ COS workers assigned to the Sangguniang Bayan Office and whose salaries are sourced from the appropriation of the Sangguniang Bayan Office. 2. Whether it is proper or not that the Municipal Vice-Mayor shall sign vouchers purchase orders/contracts for purchases of supplies and other materials funded under the office of the Sangguniang Bayan. The above-mentioned queries have been answered by this Department in its DILG Legal Opinion No. 25, dated 9 December 2016, where we opined that if the salaries of contractual/JO employees are derived from the appropriation of the Sanggunian, the City/Municipal Vice-Mayor or Vice-Governor, as the case may be, has the authority to appoint and accordingly assign them. With this, we stand with our position, upholding the Supreme Court's (SC) decision in the case of Atienza vs. Villarosal. G.R. No. 161081, IOMay2005

With respecr_ CQ issue number 2. the SC held that: "While Republic Act No. 7160 is silent as to the matter, the authority granted to the Vice-Governor to sign all warrants drawn on the provincial treasury for all expenditures appropriated for the operation of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, as well as to approve disbursement vouchers relating thereto necessarily includes the authority to approve purchase orders covering the same applying the doctrine of necessary implication. " With to issue number I. the SC held "xxx while the Governor has the authority to appoint officials and employees whose salaries are paid out of the provincial funds, this does not extend to the officials and employees of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan because such authority is lodged with the Vice-Governor. In the same manner, the authority to appoint casual and job order employees of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan belongs to the Vite- Governor. The authority of the Vice-Governor to appoint the officials and employees of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan is anchored on the fact that the salaries of these employees are derived from the appropriation specifically for the said local legislative body. the budget source ha se salarie m Io Hicials of Sangguniang Panlalawigan apart from the other employes•s and officiqls of Che province. " (Underscoring supplied for purposes of answering the query of Ms. Elizabeth C. Sayson, Secretary to the Sanggunian) Accordingly, the Memorandum issued by Mayor Glepa absolutely prohibited VM Amigo from exercising his authority to appoint the employees, whether regular or contractual/job order of the Sangguniang Bayan and restricted such authority to one of

recommendatory nature only. This clearly constituted an encroachment on the appointment power of the vice-mayor under Section 445(a)(2)2 of RA No. 7160. CC: We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Very truly yours, of the Secretary: By Autho AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary 2018-0 - RD Paisal O.
